framework: Global Geopolitical Event & Topic Coding Framework
reserved_note: Codes 11-12 are intentionally unused so that code 13 remains the start of the CAMEO conflict-escalation ladder.

axes.theme: Section A -- WHAT the document is about (subject matter). At least one required.
axes.action: Section B -- WHAT KIND of action occurred (escalation ladder). Conditional.

codes.description: Government-to-government interaction: official visits, summits, bilateral or multilateral political dialogue, diplomatic statements, and political treaties between states. Diplomacy and political relations as such -- not trade terms, not military operations, not border incidents.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes diplomatic or political relations between governments.

codes.description: Official state visits, bilateral summits, and political talks between two named governments.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a bilateral meeting or state visit between two governments.

codes.description: Engagement in multilateral bodies and regional groupings: UN votes, regional-bloc summits, joint communiques of groupings.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes multilateral diplomacy in an international organisation or regional bloc.

codes.description: Official statements, foreign-ministry briefings, ambassadorial remarks, and diplomatic signalling on political issues.
codes.hypothesis: This text reports an official government or foreign-ministry statement.

codes.description: Signing, ratification, suspension, or withdrawal from political and strategic agreements, treaties, and memoranda of understanding.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a treaty, pact, or memorandum being signed, ratified, or suspended.

codes.description: Trade, investment, and financial-policy interaction between states: tariffs, trade disputes, FDI, currency and debt arrangements, and economic sanctions. Excludes activity tied to a named connectivity initiative (code 03) and energy trade (code 04).
codes.hypothesis: This text describes trade, investment, or financial relations between countries.

codes.description: Imports and exports, tariffs, trade deficits, trade disputes, and free-trade agreements between states.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes trade flows, tariffs, or a trade agreement between countries.

codes.description: Inbound or outbound foreign direct investment, cross-border acquisitions, investment screening, and special economic zones.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes foreign investment or a cross-border acquisition.

codes.description: Currency swap lines, sovereign loans, debt restructuring, and central-bank cooperation between states.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a loan, currency swap, or debt arrangement between countries.

codes.description: Economic coercion between states: sanctions, embargoes, import bans, and export restrictions. The economic measure itself, as subject matter.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes economic sanctions or trade restrictions imposed by one country on another.

codes.description: Cross-border infrastructure, connectivity, and development-financing initiatives sponsored by any state, bloc, or multilateral body -- ports, railways, corridors, and the debt and diplomacy attached to them. Actor-neutral: applies to any sponsoring state, not one named programme.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a cross-border infrastructure or connectivity initiative.

codes.description: Ports, railways, roads, and special economic zones built under a connectivity or development initiative.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes construction of a port, railway, road, or economic zone.

codes.description: Loans, debt-sustainability concerns, defaults, and restructuring tied to initiative-linked infrastructure.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes project debt, a loan, or debt sustainability for an infrastructure project.

codes.description: A specifically named economic corridor, connectivity programme, or initiative brand referenced in reporting.
codes.hypothesis: This text names a specific economic corridor or connectivity programme.

codes.description: Initiative summits, new project agreements, and project delays, cancellations, or withdrawals.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes an infrastructure project being delayed, cancelled, or newly agreed.

codes.description: Energy interests, energy infrastructure, resource access, and energy diplomacy, including effects on partner and rival states. Energy as the subject -- pipelines, LNG, nuclear cooperation, chokepoint dependency.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes energy supply, energy infrastructure, or energy security.

codes.description: Pipelines, oil and gas supply deals, LNG contracts, and import-route dependency.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes oil or gas supply, a pipeline, or an LNG deal.

codes.description: Nuclear power plant construction or agreements, and export of renewable-energy technology.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes nuclear power or renewable energy cooperation between countries.

codes.description: Protection of, or threat to, pipelines, energy ports, refineries, and energy corridors.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a threat to, or the protection of, energy infrastructure such as a pipeline.

codes.description: Strategic competition over energy routes, resources, and maritime or overland chokepoints.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes strategic competition over energy routes or resources.

codes.description: Maritime activity in both its military/strategic and its broader maritime-affairs sense: naval operations and deployments, sea disputes, shipping lanes and chokepoints, port access, and fishing/EEZ governance.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes naval activity, a maritime dispute, or shipping and sea lanes.

codes.description: Naval deployments, port calls, patrols, and carrier or fleet movements by any state's navy.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a naval deployment, patrol, or warship movement.

codes.description: Contested waters, disputed islands and reefs, and exclusive economic zone incursions between states.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a dispute over contested waters, islands, or an exclusive economic zone.

codes.description: Strategic shipping routes, straits and chokepoints, and the security or disruption of commercial shipping.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a strategic shipping route, strait, or chokepoint.

codes.description: Overseas port leases, logistics facilities, and infrastructure with potential dual military-civilian use.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes an overseas port lease or a dual-use logistics facility.

codes.description: UNCLOS rulings and arbitration, fishing rights disputes, and blue-economy governance.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes maritime law, an UNCLOS ruling, or fishing rights.

codes.description: Defence relations BETWEEN states: joint exercises, arms transfers, force modernisation, and alliance formation. Cooperative and capability-building military activity -- not the conduct of hostilities, which is coded on the Section B escalation axis.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes defence cooperation, arms transfers, or military capability development.

codes.description: Joint military exercises, defence dialogues, staff talks, and officer exchanges between states.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a joint military exercise or defence dialogue between countries.

codes.description: Weapons transfers, defence procurement contracts, and military equipment sales between states.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes an arms sale or defence equipment deal.

codes.description: A state's force modernisation, new weapons systems, and defence capability build-up.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes military modernisation or a new weapons capability.

codes.description: Formal or informal security alignments, defence pacts, and security partnerships between states.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a security alliance, defence pact, or military partnership.

codes.description: Land-border developments between neighbouring states: disputed sectors, border infrastructure, confidence-building talks, and border incidents. Land borders specifically -- maritime boundaries are code 05.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a land border between countries.

codes.description: Disputed border sectors, competing territorial claims, and standoffs along a contested land border.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a disputed land border or territorial claim.

codes.description: Road, rail, and settlement construction near a border, including dual-use border villages.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes construction of roads, rail, or settlements near a border.

codes.description: Special-representative talks, hotline mechanisms, disengagement and de-escalation agreements on a border.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes border talks, a disengagement agreement, or a confidence-building measure.

codes.description: Skirmishes, incursions, patrol face-offs, and firing incidents at a land border.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a skirmish, incursion, or face-off at a border.

codes.description: Internal conflict, insurgency, or political instability within a state, and the role played by any external state or non-state actor -- mediation, support, or influence -- plus a state's own external messaging about its internal stability. Actor-neutral: no specific country is privileged.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes internal conflict or instability within a country.

codes.description: An outside state or organisation acting as mediator, broker, or facilitator in another country's conflict.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes an outside country mediating or brokering talks in another country's conflict.

codes.display: External Support to State / Non-state Actors
codes.description: Reported or alleged external backing of a government or of armed factions in a conflict zone.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes an outside country backing a government or armed group in a conflict.

codes.description: A government's external messaging about its own internal unrest, and international reaction to it.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes political unrest or instability inside one country.

codes.description: Conflict spilling across a border, displacement, and refugee flows affecting neighbouring states.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes refugees or conflict spilling across a border into a neighbouring country.

codes.description: Technology exports, digital-infrastructure projects, cyber activity, and influence exerted through technological means: 5G and telecom, undersea cables, surveillance technology, cyber operations, and export controls on strategic technology.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes technology, digital infrastructure, or cyber activity between countries.

codes.description: 5G rollout, telecom network contracts, undersea cables, and data-centre projects across borders.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes telecom networks, 5G, undersea cables, or data centres.

codes.description: Export or transfer of surveillance systems, facial recognition, and policing technology.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes export or transfer of surveillance or facial-recognition technology.

codes.description: Cyberattacks, cyber espionage, attribution of intrusions, and cybersecurity cooperation or dispute.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a cyberattack, cyber espionage, or cybersecurity.

codes.description: Semiconductor and technology export controls, technology-transfer restrictions, and standard-setting disputes.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes technology export controls or semiconductor restrictions.

codes.description: Humanitarian assistance, disaster relief, public-health diplomacy, and related soft-power activity by any state or organisation.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes humanitarian aid, disaster relief, or medical assistance.
codes.alertable_reason: Measured population rate 0.16% (~34 posts / 46 days, ~0.7/day) from the 872-pair judged sample, on only 4 judged positives after targeted oversampling. Too sparse to clear the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate reliably; coded for the record but not trend-alerted.

codes.description: Earthquake, flood, cyclone, or other emergency relief assistance sent across borders.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes disaster relief or emergency aid after a natural disaster.
codes.alertable_reason: inherited from parent 10: Measured population rate 0.16% (~34 posts / 46 days, ~0.7/day) from the 872-pair judged sample, on only 4 judged positives after targeted oversampling. Too sparse to clear the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate reliably; coded for the record but not trend-alerted.

codes.description: Vaccine donations, medical team deployments, and hospital construction as international assistance.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes medical assistance, vaccine donation, or health diplomacy.
codes.alertable_reason: inherited from parent 10: Measured population rate 0.16% (~34 posts / 46 days, ~0.7/day) from the 872-pair judged sample, on only 4 judged positives after targeted oversampling. Too sparse to clear the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate reliably; coded for the record but not trend-alerted.

codes.description: Aid convoys and relief delivery into an active conflict or siege setting.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes humanitarian aid being delivered into a conflict zone.
codes.alertable_reason: inherited from parent 10: Measured population rate 0.16% (~34 posts / 46 days, ~0.7/day) from the 872-pair judged sample, on only 4 judged positives after targeted oversampling. Too sparse to clear the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate reliably; coded for the record but not trend-alerted.

codes.description: Assistance programmes directed at refugee populations or migration situations.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes assistance for refugees or migrants.
codes.alertable_reason: inherited from parent 10: Measured population rate 0.16% (~34 posts / 46 days, ~0.7/day) from the 872-pair judged sample, on only 4 judged positives after targeted oversampling. Too sparse to clear the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate reliably; coded for the record but not trend-alerted.

codes.description: Threats to attack, coerce, boycott, sanction, or halt negotiations or aid unless demands are met -- including threats of force, non-force threats, and unspecified threats. The threat, not its execution.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes one party threatening another.

codes.description: Public demonstrations of dissatisfaction: demonstrations, rallies, hunger strikes, strikes and boycotts, obstruction of passage, and protests that turn violent.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a protest, demonstration, or strike.

codes.description: Military posturing short of engagement: alerts and readiness changes, mobilisation or reinforcement of police or military power, and military, naval, or air deployments and manoeuvres. Signalling capability without using it.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes a military mobilisation, alert, or show of force.

codes.description: Actions reducing the normal level of international interaction: breaking or downgrading diplomatic relations, halting aid, imposing embargoes or boycotts, ending negotiations, and expelling or withdrawing personnel.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes one country cutting ties, expelling diplomats, or halting cooperation.
codes.hypothesis_template: {actor1} reduced or severed relations with another party.
codes.alertable_reason: Measured English-cue floor 1.2% of usable-text posts (~245 posts, ~5/day). Marginal against the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate; coded for the record but excluded from daily alerting to avoid a mostly-empty panel.

codes.description: Actions to pressure or force a change in behaviour: seizing or damaging property, administrative sanctions, arrests, detentions and expulsions of individuals, and violation of territory.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes arrests, detentions, seizures, or a blockade.
codes.hypothesis_template: {actor1} detained, seized, or coerced another party.

codes.description: Physical acts of violence, sabotage, or hijacking, and lethal or non-lethal attacks that do not amount to sustained fighting. Discrete attacks rather than continuous combat.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes an attack, bombing, or act of sabotage.

codes.description: Open, extensive, continuous militarised conflict: conventional military force, blockades, occupation of territory, engagements with small or heavy weapons, violent repression, and cyberwarfare. Sustained combat rather than a single attack.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes sustained armed fighting, shelling, or military occupation.

codes.description: Use of weapons of mass destruction, and mass expulsion, mass killing, ethnic cleansing, or genocide.
codes.hypothesis: This text describes mass killing, ethnic cleansing, genocide, or use of weapons of mass destruction.
codes.hypothesis_template: {actor1} committed mass violence against a population.
codes.alertable_reason: Measured English-cue floor 0.3% of usable-text posts (~52 posts, ~1.1/day). Structurally cannot clear the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate over this window, so it would produce a permanently empty alert panel. Still coded -- an atrocity claim belongs in the record even when it cannot be trend-alerted.
